title: Scanning an apartment with an iPhone

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Will this desk fit? Before buying furniture, Antoine's household answered that by walking through their apartment with an iPhone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a phone? Not a tape measure?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Both, actually. In January 2024 they used Rhino on iPhone with LiDAR, the depth sensor on recent iPhones. It captures depth quickly, and Rhino turns it into a 3D shape you can orbit on the phone and measure roughly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's like a quick 3D sketch of the apartment.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's a good way to see it. It's not for permit drawings. It's for what Antoine calls relative confidence: how wide the hallway is, how deep the closet is, whether a big TV wall actually works.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you scan a room?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Room by room, walking slowly while the mesh updates. No tripod, no professional rig. In the living room, the largest open area, they paused at corners so the depth camera could see both walls. They checked the TV wall against a tape measure afterward, and it landed within a few centimeters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the hallway, Antoine walked it forward and back, closing the loop at the front door. The closet scan was mostly about depth, to see whether a deep shelf would fit. In the bedroom they left the furniture in place on purpose, because clearance paths were the goal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you know the scan is good?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The live mesh is the quality gate. If you see grey patches, you walk that spot again before you export. Then in Rhino you can rotate the capture and check whether two walls are really parallel, which is faster than sending a raw mesh to a desktop for a yes or no layout question.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Handheld LiDAR plus a focused modeling app was enough for early layout exploration. If the scan helps one furniture purchase, it's already paid for the hour it took.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a model-before-you-buy habit, like his skate rack CAD and his figurine pipeline.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The write-up has stills from the capture.
